groups.description: One horizontal outlined rectangle, four complete outer sides and one vertical divider extending between its top and bottom borders. Exactly two adjacent regions, left and right, with the divider near the middle. No gaps, wires, arrows, charge signs, ticks or additional objects.
One n-form glyph inside the left region and one p-form glyph inside the right region. The pixels alone do not settle Latin/Cyrillic homographs. There is no visible plus or minus inside either region.

modernDecisions: Modern Latin n on the left and p on the right derive from the exact corrected Chinese p0273#5 prose and its complete English counterpart, not a claim of script identification from source pixels.
Straight borders, a centered divider and centered labels are modern drafting regularization. No semiconductor net-charge signs are added.

groups.description: At the top, one wide two-region rectangle, a complete central divider, n-form left glyph and p-form right glyph. A wire leaves each outer side at mid-height. Neither region has a charge sign or carrier marks.

A complete circular meter with A-form glyph sits in the upper-right series branch. Another complete circular meter with V-form glyph lies across the middle left/right branches. Both meter wires terminate at their circle contours rather than crossing their labels.

Exactly three filled junction dots: at the left middle meter branch, the right middle branch below the upper meter, and the lower-right branch beside the resistor. The middle dots are horizontally aligned; both right dots lie on the same vertical trunk.

The sample-left middle trunk descends, turns right toward the central wiper, then ends as a downward arrow contacting the top of a horizontal outlined resistor rectangle. The resistor has a separate fixed left lead and a fixed right lead. The wiper is not a fixed left-end wire.

The upper sample-left wire reaches the left middle dot. The sample-right lead goes through the upper meter to the right middle dot, then down to the lower-right dot. The resistor's left fixed lead turns down and right to a slanted hollow lower-left terminal ring; its right fixed lead reaches the right trunk, which descends and turns left to a separate hollow lower-right ring. There is an open gap between the terminals. A separate minus below the left terminal and plus below the right terminal are present. There are no battery long/short plates and no connecting line spanning that gap.

modernDecisions: Latin n and p derive from corrected Chinese p0273#5/#10 and English prose. A is the modern ammeter label from the circular series meter's circuit meaning; literal homograph ambiguity is not resolved.
V is retained as the modern voltage-meter symbol matching the visible V-form glyph. Minus/plus signs remain only at the source supply terminals; no bulk-charge labeling.
Circle regularization replaces the scan's small slanted terminal rings without changing their hollow/open status. All bends, contacts, three junction dots and the wiper topology remain.
Instructional scroll canvas640x800, actual fixed media width640px explicitly tested; labels32px. No numeric apparatus values are introduced.

groups.description: Left panel has an upward vertical axis, rightward horizontal axis starting at their intersection, an I-form current glyph, a V-form voltage glyph, an unresolved oval glyph near the origin and an a-shaped source subpart glyph below. One finite solid curve starts at the origin and rises to the right with increasing steepness, ending below/right of the vertical arrow tip. No negative-axis extension in this panel and no curve continuation arrow.

Middle panel has an upward vertical axis, a horizontal axis extending left of the origin and pointing right, I-form above, minus-V-form below the left extension, V-form below the right arrow, an unresolved oval near the origin and a be-shaped subpart mark below. One finite solid curve starts below the left horizontal extension and rises shallowly toward the origin. There is no positive-side curve or breakdown turn.

Right panel has an upward vertical axis, left horizontal extension and right-pointing arrow, I-form above, minus-V-form left, V-form right, unresolved oval near the origin and a ve-shaped subpart mark below. A finite shallow negative-side solid branch below the left extension meets the origin and continues as a finite steeply rising positive-side solid branch. The common origin and two joined branches share one frame. No breakdown branch, grid, tick or data dot.

All three panels appear horizontally together; their differing axis heights and finite endpoint positions are visible. Six axis arrowheads, four finite branches (two joined in the right panel), three oval origin glyphs, three subpart glyphs, three I-form labels, three right V-form labels and two separate left minus-V-form labels. No numbered scales, ticks, grid, measured current/voltage values or curve arrows.

modernDecisions: The oval glyphs remain unresolved in literal inventory: not definitively numeral0, Latin O or Cyrillic O. Modern 0 labels are a separate conventional coordinate-origin notation, justified because the curves meet the current/voltage axis intersections. These are not source numeric data or ticks.
The source subparts Cyrillic a/be/ve map to modern a/b/c under the lesson's notation contract, explicitly present in corrected Chinese and English references to226a/b/c.
Modern I denotes current and V denotes voltage, preserving I-form/V-form axis meaning and the source's minus signs. No I/U/V values are invented.

Bezier smoothing, clean axes and enlarged spacing are modern qualitative regularization only, not recovered numerical data. Retain every source finite branch, both shared-origin joins and solid styles, with no extension to breakdown.
